title: Lead with 'one-time purchase, no subscription'
rationale: MacCleaner Pro charges $85.95 one-time vs $39.95/yr, while DaisyDisk ($9.99) and Mole ($19) stress one-time pricing. A clear no-subscription promise may differentiate against suites that push subscriptions.

title: Price in a low-to-mid one-time band
rationale: Verified one-time prices are $9.99 (DaisyDisk), $19 (Mole) and $85.95 (MacCleaner Pro, 1 Mac). A price above DaisyDisk/Mole but well below the suite tier may read as full-featured yet fair.

title: Combine cleanup, uninstaller and disk map in one native app
rationale: Single-purpose tools are common (AppCleaner and Pearcleaner uninstall; DaisyDisk and GrandPerspective visualize). Only Mole was verified covering cleanup, uninstall and disk map together at a one-time price, so the bundle is not yet crowded.

title: Offer a free scan-first trial like Hyperspace
rationale: Hyperspace allows unlimited free scanning and charges to act; MacCleaner Pro offers only a 2-day trial. Showing reclaimable space before purchase may build trust.

title: Investigate developer-cache cleanup as a differentiator
rationale: No fetched competitor page mentioned developer-tool cleanup; the field is unknown for all competitors, which is absence of evidence, not evidence of absence. A targeted follow-up run is needed before committing.
